The '''2017–18 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team''' represented [[Villanova University]] in the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. Led by head coach [[Jay Wright (basketball)|Jay Wright]] in his 17th year, the Wildcats played their home games at the [[Wells Fargo Center (Philadelphia)|Wells Fargo Center]] in [[Philadelphia|Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]] as members of the [[Big East Conference]].

The Wildcats finished the season 36–4, 14–4 in [[2017–18 Big East Conference men's basketball season|Big East play]] to finish in second place. They defeated [[2017–18 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Marquette]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.foxsports.com/wisconsin/story/marquette-golden-eagles-falls-to-villanova-94-70-in-big-east-tournament-030818|title=Marquette falls to Villanova 94-70 in Big East tournament|date=2018-03-08|work=FOX Sports|access-date=2018-04-06|language=en-US}}</ref> [[2017–18 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team|Butler]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/butler/2018/03/09/villanova-overpowers-butler-87-68-big-east-semifinal/410925002/|title=Insider: Butler powerless against Villanova in Big East semifinal|work=Indianapolis Star|access-date=2018-04-06|language=en}}</ref> and [[2017–18 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]] to win the [[2018 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]] championship.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/03/10/villanova-tops-providence-for-2nd-straight-big-east-title/32825969/|title=Villanova tops Providence for 2nd straight Big East title|work=USA TODAY|access-date=2018-04-06|language=en}}</ref> As a result, they received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 1 seed in the East region, their third No.1 seed in four years.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/colleges/villanova/villanova-march-madness-2018-bracket-ncaa-tournament-seed-20180311.html|title=March Madness: Villanova earns No. 1 seed in East region in NCAA tournament, will play LIU-Brooklyn or Radford - Philly|work=Philly.com|access-date=2018-04-06}}</ref> They defeated [[2017–18 Radford Highlanders men's basketball team|Radford]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/college/college-basketball/ncaa-tournament-villanova-radford-march-madness-f39868|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180406230329/https://www.newsday.com/sports/college/college-basketball/ncaa-tournament-villanova-radford-march-madness-1.17412553|url-status=live|archive-date=April 6, 2018|title=Top-seeded Villanova dominates Radford|work=Newsday|access-date=2018-04-06|language=en}}</ref> [[2017–18 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401025862|title=Alabama vs. Villanova - Game Recap - March 17, 2018 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-04-06}}</ref> [[2017–18 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team|West Virginia]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/03/23/sports/ncaabasketball/villanova-west-virginia.html|title=Villanova Breaks Free of West Virginia in the Second Half to Win|last=Schonbrun|first=Zach|date=2018-03-23|work=The New York Times|access-date=2018-04-06|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> and [[2017–18 Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball team|Texas Tech]] to advance to the Final Four for the second time in three years.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/sports/wp/2018/03/25/texas-tech-takes-on-villanova-were-going-to-have-to-play-our-best-40-minutes/|title=Known as pretty, Villanova is gritty in knocking out Texas Tech to reach Final Four|last1=Stubbs|first1=Roman|date=2018-03-25|newspaper=Washington Post|access-date=2018-04-06|last2=Boren|first2=Cindy|language=en-US|issn=0190-8286}}</ref> In the National Semifinal, they defeated [[2017–18 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/03/31/sports/final-four-villanova-kansas.html|title=Villanova Rolls Over Kansas to Reach Its Second N.C.A.A. Final in Three Seasons|last=Schonbrun|first=Zach|date=2018-03-31|work=The New York Times|access-date=2018-04-06|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/04/01/villanova-beats-kansas-final-four-march-madness-national-championship|title=Villanova overpowers Kansas from three in Final Four rout|work=SI.com|access-date=2018-04-06|language=en}}</ref> before defeating [[2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] in the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|National Championship game]] to win their second national championship in three years.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401025888|title=Michigan vs. Villanova - Game Recap - April 2, 2018 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-04-06}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2018/04/03/ncaa-title-game-michigan-villanova/480762002/|title=Michigan basketball can't solve Villanova, special season terminated|work=Detroit Free Press|access-date=2018-04-06|language=en}}</ref> They won every game of the tournament by a double-digit margin and the team's tournament run is widely considered one of the most dominant ever along with being called among the best seasons of all time.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/the-only-opponent-villanova-has-left-is-history/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180403162259/https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/the-only-opponent-villanova-has-left-is-history/|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 3, 2018|title=The Only Opponent Villanova Has Left Is History|last=Paine|first=Neil|date=2018-04-03|work=FiveThirtyEight|access-date=2018-04-06|language=en-US}}</ref>

The Wildcats' home court, [[Finneran Pavilion|The Pavilion]], underwent a temporary closure for a $60 million renovation project during the season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.phillymag.com/news/2017/02/16/villanova-pavilion-renovation-basketball-gym/|title=Villanova Plans $60 Million Makeover of Pavilion|date=2017-02-16|work=Philadelphia Magazine|access-date=2017-07-14|language=en-US}}</ref> It reopened for the 2018–19 season with the new name of Finneran Pavilion after a Villanova alum who donated $22.6 million to Villanova.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.villanova.com/genrel/021417aac.html |title=Board of Trustees Approves Pavilion Renovation |publisher=[[Villanova Wildcats]] |date=February 14, 2017 |access-date=March 30, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.vuhoops.com/2017/2/14/14612240/villanova-basketball-finneran-pavilion-renovation-announced-60-million|title=Villanova Basketball Pavilion Renovation Approved|work=VU Hoops|access-date=2017-07-14}}</ref> Accordingly, all home games for the 2017–18 season but one were played at the Wells Fargo Center.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.villanova.com/genrel/021417aac.html|title=Board of Trustees Approves Pavilion Renovation|access-date=2017-07-14|language=en}}</ref> The exception was the November 29, 2017 game with [[Philadelphia Big 5|Big 5]] rival [[2017-18 Penn Quakers men's basketball team|Penn]]; it was instead held at [[Jake Nevin Field House]], which had been home to the team before the Pavilion's initial 1986 opening.<ref>{{cite press release |url=http://www.villanova.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/090117aaa.html |title=Wildcats to Host Penn in Jake Nevin Field House |publisher=[[Villanova Wildcats]] |date=September 1, 2017 |access-date=September 12, 2017 |archive-date=September 12, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170912102614/http://www.villanova.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/090117aaa.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Previous season==
The [[2016–17 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Wildcats]] finished the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17 season]] 32–4, 15–3 in [[2016–17 Big East Conference men's basketball season|Big East play]] to win the regular season championship. In the [[2017 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]], they defeated [[2016–17 St. John's Red Storm men's basketball team|St. John's]], [[2016–17 Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball team|Seton Hall]], and [[2016–17 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]] to win the tournament championship.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/big-east-tournament-2017-scores-bracket-live-blog-villanova-to-face-creighton-in-title-game/|title=Big East tournament 2017 scores, bracket: Villanova makes statement with dominant title win|work=CBSSports.com|access-date=2017-07-14|language=en}}</ref> As a result, they received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. The Wildcats were given the Tournament's overall No. 1 seed as a No. 1 seed in the East region. In the First Round they defeated [[2016–17 Mount St. Mary's Mountaineers men's basketball team|Mount St. Mary's]] before being upset by No. 8-seeded [[2016–17 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]] in the Second Round.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2017/03/18/wisconsin-villanova-badgers-wildcats-upset-ncaa-tournament|title=Down goes Villanova: No. 8 seed Wisconsin stuns the reigning national champs|last=Greene|first=Dan|work=SI.com|access-date=2017-07-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/march-finally-gives-us-some-madness-as-wisconsin-ousts-villanova-3-takeaways/|title=March finally gives us some madness as Wisconsin ousts Villanova: 3 takeaways|work=CBSSports.com|access-date=2017-07-14|language=en}}</ref> The loss marked the second time in the previous three tournaments that Villanova was upset by an eighth-seeded team.

== Preseason ==
In its annual preseason preview, Blue Ribbon Yearbook ranked the Wildcats No. 12 in the country.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://blueribbonyearbook.com/blogs/news/arizona-tops-blue-ribbons-37th-annual-preseason-rankings|title=Arizona Tops Blue Ribbon's 37th Annual Preseason Rankings|work=Blue Ribbon College Basketball Yearbook|access-date=2017-09-20}}</ref> [[Jalen Brunson]] was named a third team preseason All-American.<ref name=":0" />

Villanova was picked to win the Big East in the conference's preseason Coaches' Poll for the fourth consecutive year.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.bigeast.com/news/2017/10/18/mens-basketball-villanova-sits-atop-coaches-preseason-poll-again.aspx|title=Big East Conference – Villanova Sits Atop Coaches' Preseason Poll Again|website=www.bigeast.com|language=en|access-date=2017-10-22}}</ref> Jalen Brunson was named the unanimous preseason All-Big East player of the year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bigeast.com/news/2017/10/18/mens-basketball-villanovas-jalen-brunson-selected-preseason-player-of-the-year.aspx|title=Big East Conference – Villanova's Jalen Brunson Selected Preseason Player of the Year|website=www.bigeast.com|language=en|access-date=2017-10-22}}</ref>
